I. S. Lupinovich Belarusian Agricultural Library of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
records.summary: A brief history and activities of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) as the UN specialized agency for food security and the world's leading publisher are reviewed. The unique character of the institutional FAO Knowledge Repository, the timeliness and relevance of FAO publications presented in the public domain, their importance for researchers and specialists in agriculture are emphasized with the brief review of the publications. The role of the Belarusian Agricultural Library as FAO national depository, its participation in FAO projects is highlighted.

records.title: The local lore section of the library website based on IRBIS64 database Memorable Data Calendar
records.summary: The author discusses the experience of the centralized library system in building the local lore section of the library’s website based on WebIrbis64r_plus and acquiring the factographic database “Memorable Data Calendar”. She demonstrates the options of representing personalia, memorable and jubilee dates, as well as describes the search options and the website subject-oriented sections. The author also emphasizes the role of professional librarians in building the website section.

records.title: The information system to control current scientific activities at the Federal Research Center of Information and Computational Technologies
authors: Federal Research Center of Information and Computational Technologies
Federal Research Center of Information and Computational Technologies
Federal Research Center of Information and Computational Technologies
Federal Research Center of Information and Computational Technologies
Federal Research Center of Information and Computational Technologies
records.summary: The authors examine the issues of further development of the information system of current scientific activities control at the Federal Research Center of Information and Computational Technologies, and suggest the upgraded model for scientific publications based on several basic principles. They discuss in detail the approach to information retrieval and extraction based on the abstract model of attributes and expressive intuitive query language. The in-house machine-readable format enables to solve the applied problems, e. g. data export/import, data transformation into standard formats, and report generation.

records.title: The career fair to facilitate employment of the graduates
authors: Vladimir Regional Colleges of Culture and Arts
records.summary: The author examines the efficient forms to facilitate employment of the graduates from vocational educational organizations, and the career fair in particular. She examines the main vectors of collegeemployers interaction and discusses the experience of the Career Center of Vladimir Regional College of Culture and Arts. She shares the experience of Career Fair of Jobs and Training Places “Your choice – your opportunities” held annually at Vladimir Regional College of Culture and Arts.

records.title: The RAS Library’s for Natural Sciences digital services: The status and prospects
authors: Library for Natural Sciences, Russian Academy of Sciences
records.summary: The author reviews the digital services of the Library for Natural Sciences that provide comfort and accessibility for the users. The library information system TopAZ is the core of the digital services system and Electronic Library of LNS RAS. The prospects for the library’s digital services are linked with the further implementation of new technologies, e.g. AI, and the data processing tools to enhance information retrieval, advance of web-based services to support access to the library resources and scientific data instruments.

records.title: Professional skill competitions in the system of mid-level training
authors: St. Petersburg College of Library and Information Technologies
records.summary: Every specialty requires mastering a set of skills and competences to be acquired through practical and theoretical training. It is reasonable to assess the quality of training mid-level specialists through the lens of their striving for personal growth. The competitions of professional skills are to reveal this motivation. The competitions differ in their characteristics, they may be internal and external, meanwhile their key value lies in advancing professional thinking, motivation of young specialists to stay and develop in the library industry.

records.title: Portal of sectoral electronic catalogs based on IRBIS128. Experience of the Belarusian Agricultural Library
authors: I. S. Lupinovich Belarusian Agricultural Library of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
I. S. Lupinovich Belarusian Agricultural Library of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
I. S. Lupinovich Belarusian Agricultural Library of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
records.summary: The authors describe the experience of creating the portal of sectoral electronic catalogs on the basis of IRBIS128, which facilitates interaction between libraries and research and practice centers, as well as the creation and sharing of bibliographic databases. The authors review users’ interaction with the union electronic catalog of the Department of Agrarian Sciences of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus and with individual electronic catalog of the participating libraries that apply the functional capabilities of IRBIS system to create, edit and manage bibliographic records.

records.title: Popularizing scientific knowledge in the Library for Natural Sciences of the Russian Academy of Sciences
authors: Library for Natural Sciences, Russian Academy of Sciences
records.summary: The author discusses the need to build knowledge in the natural sciences and the humanities in children and teenagers and motivate their research initiative. As the case study of the RAS Library for Natural Sciences, she analyzes the key approaches of the libraries aimed at science popularization among younger generation. The author argues that interaction with RAS research institutions and users is the specific feature of this activity. She reviews in brief the RAS LNS’ rare book collection used in educational projects and excursions.

records.title: Organization’s publication activity. Acquisition and use of the database of employees’ publications
authors: Osipyan Institute of Solid State Physics
records.summary: The institutional sci-tech libraries and research organizations’ information departments are in charge of acquiring data on employees’ publications, analyzing the array of publications and maintaining their control. The academic organizations and research institutions are accountable for publication output and have to monitor the dynamics of users information needs. The international scientometrical databases have restricted the access to the functions used to assess organizational performance and to generate reports before 2022. The national providers (National Electronic Library, academic publishers, etc.) provide data with serious delay. In these circumstances, the institutional resources and accumulated data are vitally important.

records.title: New versions of RNPLS&T’s terminological dictionaries and approaches to acquire them
authors: Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
records.summary: The authors discuss the RNPLS&T’s system of electronic terminological dictionaries with the focus on the new versions and their distinctive features. They describe the subject scope, sources and comprised terms as well as the type structure of the dictionary database and dictionaries’ functionality. The approaches and principles of the acquisition are analyzed. The authors emphasize the significance of the dictionaries for the professionals in the library and information business, information technologies and artificial intelligence. The paper is prepared under the Government Order for RNPLS&T for 2025 No. 075-00548-25-00, Project No. 720000F.99.1.BN60AV03000, theme No. 1024031400219-9-5.8.3 (FNEG-2025-0006).

records.title: Library information services and artificial intelligence: Key focuses in scientific publications
records.summary: The author reviews the library scientific publications related to artificial intelligence (AI). She concludes that while some authors speculate of AI potential for the libraries, the others threat with AI possible risks. The author analyzes publications on the AI implementation into library practice and librarians’ learning new competences to apply AI instruments.

records.title: Library and information professional training: Problems and prospects
records.summary: The author discusses the library professional education at the institutes of culture. Based on the 2014-2024 publications, she selected 313 papers within the mentioned subject scope. The qualitative and quantitative characteristics are found for the document flow. Basic problems of library training in the recent decade are generalized. The most prospective themes and trends in the library information activities are identified on the basis of “Libcom-2024” Program.

records.title: Integrating departmental systems of publication performance analysis with institutional information systems
records.summary: The author examines the problems of informatization of academic organizations, with the focus on accumulation and efficient utilization of institutional information resources, in particular when designing software applications. The author shares the experience of the information system “Analysis of publication performance” designed to accumulate data on research output of the employees. The author emphasizes that in designing the system, the issues of using the institutional accumulated information resources (data integration) for developing specialized services of administrative services were addressed data coherency permitting.

records.title: Improving the quality and efficiency of information services for remote users of Belarus Agricultural Library through the development and implementation of specialised software complexes
authors: I. S. Lupinovich Belarus Agricultural Library, National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
I. S. Lupinovich Belarus Agricultural Library, National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
I. S. Lupinovich Belarus Agricultural Library, National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
I. S. Lupinovich Belarus Agricultural Library, National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
records.summary: The authors discuss the characteristics of two software packages and their implementation into bibliographic services for remote users of Belarus Agricultural Library. The service consists of user and administrative blocks. The user block contains information and queries. The administrative block includes several main modules: user accounts, queries, monitoring and statistics. In January 2025, the module for “list generation” will be implemented into the user and administrative blocks. The specialized software packages enable employees servicing users to monitor the required information in some resources in a semi-automatic mode and transmit information to the end user, to receive requests for document delivery, deliver full texts of requested documents, to finalize bibliographic lists and to display graphically the characteristics of documents from already generated bibliographic lists. The implementation of this system will be the largest update to the remote user services of Belarus Agricultural Library over the past ten years.

records.title: Formation and use of the Authority file “Individual Authors” in IRBIS64+ Library Automation System (the case study of Belarus Agricultural Library)
authors: I. S. Lupinovich Belarusian Agricultural Library of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus
records.summary: Within the framework of the project of acquiring the corporate database “Agrarian Scientists of Belarus”, the experience of the Belarusian Agricultural Library (hereinafter BelAL) in creating authoritative/ normative records for the names of persons in the ATHRA database – Authority File ‘Individual Authors’ in the Library Automation System IRBIS64+ is discussed. The stages of work and status of the project are described. The author reviews the practical guide “The authority file “Individual Authors” of Library Automation System IRBIS64+ (ATHRA database): The procedure” (Minsk, 2023), prepared by BelAL experts. The guide comprises the rules of filling-in the fields / subfields in the main worksheet “ATHRA1 – worksheet for entering authority / master record on Individual Authors’’ in accordance with the methodological solutions adopted by BelAL. The author also discusses using the Authority File “Individual Authors” in the current cataloging and updating of bibliographic records in the electronic catalog and other library’s databases.

records.title: Factors of library’s operation within the partner schools cooperation
records.summary: The author examines the significance of strong partnership with the focus to computerization. She also discusses the problems of children’s interest toward reading.

records.title: Developing master version of the State Rubricator of Scientific and Technical Information: Subject classes 37 Geophysiccs, 38 Geology, and 39 Geography
authors: Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
records.summary: The authors introduce the findings of the research project to develop and update the subject contents and structural organization of Classes 37 Geophysics, 38 Geology, and 39 Geography of the SRSTI-2022 amended in 2023. The purpose is to prepare proposals for the SRSTI master version 2025. Within the geophysical sciences, the authors suggest to introduce 14 new subject headings and to change the names of 5 headings. Within the geological sciences, they suggest to introduce 45 new subject headings and to change14 names. For geographical sciences, 2 new subject headings are proposed to be introduced with 2 changes of names. To develop the polyhierarchical links between the SRSTI subject headings, 10 “see also”, 30 “see”, 4 “eq.”, 30 “ref. from” links have to be added. With the proposed changes, the corresponding fragments of updated SRSTI Classification Table are constructed. The paper is prepared within the framework of the Government Order to RNPLS&T for 2025 No. 075-00548-25-00, Project No. 720000F.99.1.BN60AA03000, theme No. 1024052200005-7-1.2.1;5.8.2 (FNEG-2025-0008).

records.title: Designing storage subsystems as the case study of HAC Electronic Archive
authors: Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
records.summary: The authors examine the document information system of the Higher Attestation Commission (HAC) Archive and discuss, in particular, design and development of the storage subsystem that would enable to improve the system and document processing, search and storage. For this purpose, the electronic database of HAC document archive was acquired. The applied methods are suggested as the universal methodology for building subsystems for storing document information in electronic archives. The paper is prepared under the Government Order for RNPLS&T for 2025, theme “Organizational, technological and technical support of document digitization, development and updating of HAC digital document archive, verification of bibliographic data of scientific publications using effective complex of bibliometric and abstract databases”

records.title: Designing chatbot to provide methodological support of the libraries
authors: Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
records.summary: In 2024, RNPLS&T has initiated designing methodological chatbot to support sci-tech libraries using Telegram chat communication as the popular format of online communication. The authors characterize the types of chat communication and the goals of using chatbots in libraries. They define the tasks to be addressed by the methodological chatbots, the chatbot structure, and describe the instruments used to design the methodological chatbot. The paper is prepared under the Government Order for RNPLS&T for 2025 No. 075-00548-25-00, Project No. 720000F.99.1.BN60AV03000, theme No. 1024031400219-9-5.8.3 (FNEG-2025-0006).

records.title: Cognitive approach to designing user interface of departmental information systems of publication performance analysis
authors: Institute of Psychology, Russian Academy of Sciences
records.summary: The author discusses the approach to designing user interface of departmental information system of publication performance analysis. The approach is based on the study and analysis of human cognitive activity within the process of interaction with user interface. The brief description of departmental information system of publication performance analysis is provided. The author examines the user accounts and functional roles and formulates the two vectors of human component to be considered in designing information system user interface. The cognitive activity approach is chosen as the methodological foundation of considering the human aspect in designing user interface. The publication is prepared within the framework of the Government Order No. 0138-2022-0010 “Regulation of professional interaction in the circumstances of organizational and technological challenges”.

records.title: Building the system to acquire and analyze data on the information needs of the Bank of Russia
records.summary: The author describes the process of design and implementation of the subsystem of computerized acquisition and analysis of data related to the Bank’s of Russia information needs in periodicals, i.e., the workstation “Subscription Workstation”. The demand for the subsytem is evidenced by the annual study of Bank divisions information needs. The process of design and development was based on the functionality requirements to the upgraded Information Library Complex automated system. The subsystem advantages and prospects are discussed.

records.title: Bibliographic culture as a factor of public Internet safety
records.summary: The author examines the problem of low bibliographic culture of the Internet resources as a symptom of spontaneous mass “safety dysfunction” of authors, publicators, and the audience. This is caused by the popular illusion of the Internet communication as supposedly unsafe environment of maximum opportunities and freedom in the circumstances of developing national Internet segments as the fragments of the transborder global network at the expense of digital sovereignty, to an even greater degree. Lacking reliable public instruments to verify personality of authors and publicators, as well as the institutionalofficial data, optionality of reliable bibliographic record of publication have made mass Internet users vulnerable against fraud, cheating, deceptive practices, falsifications of traditional values and political disinformation. Since 2014, and to an even greater degree since 2022, the imperious necessity urges to enhance state regulation of bibliographic records reliability for Internet-based resources, to build and develop appropriate mass culture, and thus to ensure the safety of public Internet communications. The paper is prepared under the Government Order by the RF Ministry of Science and Higher Education “Fundamental studies of theoretical backgrounds of contemporary sociality (social physics 5.0) including advancing mathematical methods of cognitive mechanisms actualization and modelling social processes” (FSZZ-2024-0010), No. 1024062800006-5-2.2.3;1.2.1;5.4.1;1.7.1.

records.title: AI in the libraries around the globe: The analytical review
authors: Russian National Public Library for Science and Technology
National Research University “Higher School of Economics”
records.summary: The analytical review of AI in the libraries of the world is focused on the practice of large national and academic libraries in several European and Asian countries, in particular on 135 projects. The authors report that AI is used in foreign libraries for symbol recognition, difficult languages, historical documents, and visual materials. The AI is indispensable in complex and fast metadata processing, analysis and classification. In the library integrated systems, AI not only processes user queries, it upgrades information retrieval and tunes personal recommendations. The authors offer their recommendations on integrating AI into the library systems and on how to develop and use efficiently AI functionality in the library search systems. The paper is prepared under the Government Order for RNPLS&T for 2025 No. 075-00548-25-00, Project No. 720000F.99.1.BN60AA03000, theme No. 1024031200035-5-1.2.1;5.8.2 (FNEG-2025-0004).

records.title: 6-НК краткая: организация межведомственной системы федерального статистического наблюдения
authors: Main Information and Computing Center, Ministry of Culture of the Russian Federation
Main Information and Computing Center, Ministry of Culture of the Russian Federation
records.summary: The authors examine the problems of state statistical control of libraries. The goal is to build the uniform system for acquiring data on the national librarianship. They discuss the procedures and stages of control organization, formulate genre-specific typology of the libraries to be statistically monitored, specify stages of the project and evaluate the challenges.

records.title: Would Self-Supported Fracture Contribute to the Hydrocarbon Production in Shale Reservoir Besides Proppant-Supported Fracture
records.summary: Abstract During hydraulic fracturing in deep shale gas reservoirs, it is difficult to pump proppants long distances, and self-supported fractures are formed at the far and upper ends of the fractures. The self-supported fracture could hold the fracture space by its surface structure again fracture closure. However, it faces various aspects of impairment during shale gas reservoir development, which affect its conductivity. Among the impairment, long-term production results in a decline of bottom hole pressure, which will compact the fracture space, and self-supported fractures without proppant are more sensitive than those with proppant. In this paper, we conducted a series of experiments with samples from a deep shale gas reservoir in the Sichuan basin of China. The self-supported fracture conductivity behavior at high temperatures and high-pressure conditions was studied from the aspects of various fracture dislocation distances, pressure reduction methods, and well-open and shut-in times. Then, the mechanism of self-supported fracture impairment was revealed from the change in fracture width, fracture surface roughness, and fracture surface microscopic morphology. With the ideal numerical model, the impact of self-supported fracture ratio, and pressure drop methods on the gas production were analyzed. The results indicate that the dislocation of self-supported fractures can improve its conductivity greatly. The self-supported fracture conductivity with 1 mm dislocation was increased by 18.5 times to 76.1 times compared with those without dislocation. With the production continuing, when the net pressure on the self-supported fractures is above 35 MPa, its conductivity was impaired significantly, reaching 51.2-92.0%. Small pressure reduction step/more frequent nozzle replacement and reducing the well open and shut-in times would help protect the self-supported fracture conductivity. When the net pressure on self-supported fractures increased from 10 MPa to 30 MPa, the equivalent width of fractures decreased by 53.3%. The average height of the fracture surface decreased by 30.7% after pressure compaction. The numerical modeling study indicates that the larger the volume of self-supported fractures, the higher the productivity of the gas well. In a 3-year production time, when the ratio of proppant-supported fractures to self-supported fractures increased from 1:0.25 to 1:5, the cumulative gas production increased by 220.8% (90.7×106). The small-pressure drop production has higher cumulative productivity than the high-pressure drop method. The cumulative gas production is 115.2×106 when a 10 MPa pressure drop is used, while it is 80.9 ×106 with a 50 MPa pressure drop. This study could provide a theoretical basis for hydraulic fracturing and production system optimization of deep shale gas reservoirs.

records.title: World's Largest Non-Traditional Packer with Extreme Annulus Sealability
records.summary: Abstract The historical use of packers in the oil and gas industry has primarily involved elastomers with hydraulic or mechanical operating systems. Bismuth alloy technology offers an alternative material with a distinct operating system. TDAP stands for thermally deformable annulus packer which is a non-traditional seal that aids in sealing leakages in an annulus with Sustained Casing Pressure as a preventative solution before the pressure is observed at the surface. The technology was developed with extensive lab, yard, and field testing to prove the reliability of this alloy, particularly for larger annulus spaces, such as 9 5/8″ × 13 3/8″. The objective is to proactively eliminate the risk of Sustained Casing Pressure (SCP) in the production and intermediate casing annuli. The method used to demonstrate this system's applicability involves having bismuth alloy disks on the exterior of one joint of the 9 5/8″ casing. The joint is positioned to achieve the intended depth for the packer. The packer is set above the 13 3/8″ shoe. After cementing, the disks are turned into a liquid using a heater run inside the 9 5/8″ casing. This heater is precisely controlled for temperature and optimized for heat transfer. When the heat source is removed, the bismuth alloy solidifies between the intermediate and production casing, creating a metal-to-metal annulus seal - steel to bismuth alloy to steel. Bismuth has minor expansion properties which give the packer gas tight qualities. To succeed in the field trial, this system underwent testing under full downhole conditions. The setup mimicked the pressure, temperature, casing design, and the medium in which the alloy is set downhole. The test included the heater deployment, the melting of the alloy, and pressure testing of the system up to 5,000 psi in hydraulic pressure. A unique sealing mechanism of bismuth alloy proactively prevents SAP B. The paper describes the results of the extensive R&D work undertaken, during which the annular bismuth alloy barriers were tested and withstood up to a 5,000-psi pressure differential, having been formed in drilling fluid, clear brine, and cement. The success of the implementation in the world's largest offshore field will be described. In particular, the innovative well design and deployment of the annular packer to be set in clear brine for maximum pressure integrity with a gas-tight rated seal will be highlighted. This is the industry's first downhole utilization of bismuth alloys for this size with this application. Its novelty lies not only in the size but also in the engineering required to achieve optimal heat transfer and alloy melting efficiency for such a large size, which entails carefully studying the behavior of this untraditional alloy.

records.title: When Conventional ESP Meets the Unconventional Limit: Putting More Power Downhole Safely
records.summary: Permanent magnet motors (PMM) have been around for two decades in the electrical submersible pumps (ESP) industry. PMM are shorter-lighter-higher power density in design and offer more than just energy savings with reduced carbon footprint; it is a technology enabler to achieve asset optimization and yet is underutilized. This paper discusses the early reporting on the first company organic PMM safely installed in a Permian Basin unconventional resource well to extract more reservoir production. The benefit to the reader is stronger confidence to apply this green technology in their wells safely and economically. To achieve sustainable first use of PMM, the ESP design and safety implications required collaboration of disciplines involving teams of Instrumentation & Electrical, Production and Completion engineers, the ESP Center of Excellence, the Technical Center, Health-Safety-Environmental, and a variety of vendors over a 2-year period. Pump design and drawdown scenarios were examined while multiple safety trainings were conducted, including live demonstrations with PPE, proving the safe mitigation of hazardous voltage through proper shunting, grounding, and isolating standard operating procedures. Additionally, multiple safety devices were added (surface and subsurface) to manage the safety aspects of this technology. A final risk assessment was conducted and approved to clear the way for PMM installation. Compared to the conventional induction motor, the PMM enabled nearly 50% more power downhole for equal fluid density, comparable production and water cut without a change in pump design. Energy savings and carbon footprint reduction is 19%. Since installation, the ESP system has reduced head pressure more than 300 psi and continues to see increased production. Standard operating procedures for PMM were executed successfully and safely without incident using the free hub second source power mitigator. Four electrical technologies are included in this paper for safety of personnel and the asset as PMM bring the risk of electrical shock due to two sources of power: planned power from the grid and unplanned power from the well; the latter case the PMM is a generator and this risk is mitigated with the use of both completion and production tools such as the free hub. Additionally, the non-intrusive power measurement technology at the surface keeps personnel safe from arc-flash and electrical shock without the use of cumbersome CAT-2 PPE, a health risk in hot climates. A contactor switch at the surface helps to protect life and asset. Lastly, a common mode filter was run for carrier frequencies less than 4000 Hz to reduce or eliminate high frequency induced failures such as bearing fluting.

records.title: Wettability Quantification in Organic-Rich Mudrocks by Water Adsorption Isotherms
records.summary: Abstract A precise wettability assessment of organic-rich mudrocks (ORM) is still an ongoing challenge. The intricate complex composition of these rocks is one of the aspects that complicates quantification of wettability of ORM. In this paper, we introduce a new method to experimentally estimate wettability of complex reservoir rocks by utilizing water adsorption isotherm measurements. We also verify the reliability of this method by comparing it against conventional wettability assessment methods. Moreover, we assess the influence of mineral composition and Total Organic Content (TOC) on the measured water adsorption isotherms. Powdered rock samples collected from two ORM formations, A and B, and a carbonate formation were used for a set of experimental measurements. X-ray diffraction (XRD) was performed to obtain weight concentrations of mineral components. TOC was quantified using pyrolysis measurements and EDS measurements were carried out to analyze the spatial distribution of rock components. Then, we performed N2 adsorption- desorption measurements to obtain the surface area of the solid components in the samples. Water adsorption isotherms were computed using a Dynamic Vapor Sorption Analyzer and water contact angle was measured using a goniometer. Two carbonate samples were added to the set of rocks analyzed for the purpose of comparison and verification of the results. One of the carbonate samples was kept on its original water-wet state and the other sample was chemically modified to render an oil-wet sample. The water adsorption isotherms performed on the ORM samples were compared against water contact angle measurements. Results demonstrated that the three samples from formation A that displayed overlapping water adsorption isotherms also present very similar contact angle, indicating that they have similar affinity to water. The sample from formation A that showed the lowest water adsorption was found to have the highest contact angle among the samples from formation A, underscoring its low affinity to water. Contact angle measurements obtained for the water-wet and the chemically-altered oil-wet carbonate samples were 0° and 120°, respectively. The Amott index of the unmodified carbonate sample was 0.5. After wettability alteration, it decreased to 0, indicating a mixed-wet behavior. However, water adsorption isotherms show only 25% decrease at 70% relative humidity, suggesting a moderate change in the wettability towards the oil-wet state. Both isotherms and Amott index agrees that the sample did not reach a completely oil-wet behavior, while contact angle measurements suggest a significantly oil-wet state. We demonstrated that water adsorption isotherms effectively capture changes in wettability resulting from alterations in the composition of the rock. Our results also revealed that the introduced method effectively identifies the different wetting characteristics of reservoir rocks. By quantifying water adsorption isotherms, we can overcome challenges such as surface roughness/contamination that often lead to uncertainties in contact angle measurements. It also eliminates the limitations of imbibition-based method, which makes them unreliable in tight rocks. The technique introduced here can be used as a new method of wettability characterization that honors the complex geochemistry of ORM.

records.title: Wellbore Stability Uncertainty Quantification Using a Bayesian Machine Learning Framework
records.summary: Abstract One of the major challenges in wellbore stability analysis is to quantify the uncertainty of the mud weight window and provide probabilities of breakouts and drilling induced tensile fractures for a given mud weight. Modeling the safe drilling window requires many geomechanics inputs, such as: rock strength, elastic properties, in-situ stresses, pore pressure, etc. Most of these inputs are calculated using empirical correlations based on limited test data; or calculated using simple elastic equations and calibrated with limited data points. Uncertainties in test and calibration data combined with uncertainties in correlations make it exceedingly difficult to correctly assess the uncertainty of the resulting safe drilling window. An accurate quantification of measurement and other input uncertainties and correct propagation of uncertainty throughout the modeling process can improve decision quality and wellbore instability related non-productive time and drilling costs. Geomechanics modeling of a complex physical system requires a solid understanding of fundamental physics and domain expertise. However, current uncertainty methods often lack a mathematically rigorous framework that can integrate both physics and domain expertise into the modeling process. To address the challenges mentioned above, a Bayesian machine learning framework has been adopted as the foundation of our physics-based uncertainty workflow, which allows to incorporate prior information from domain knowledge and fundamental physics, to integrate collected lab and field measurement data into the modeling process, and to improve the model using an iterative workflow. The resulting workflow can account for the complex interrelationships and interactions between different components in the geomechanics system; specifically, the capability to model and calibrate the uncertainties for several essential components underlying the one-dimensional wellbore stability model. These components include geomechanical core tests and stress measurements (such as Leak-off Test (LOT), Extended Leak-off Test (XLOT), Diagnostic Fracture Injection Tests (DFIT), etc.), as well as drilling performance (such as mud weight used, appearance of breakout and drilling induced tensile fractures, etc.). This workflow provides a systematic and consistent framework for evaluating uncertainty in building a 1D Mechanical Earth Model (1DMEM) which is a crucial step in ensuring a safe and efficient drilling process. We will demonstrate this uncertainty quantification workflow and its application for estimating the safe drilling windows with a case study.

records.title: Video-Powered AI Solutions for Active Monitoring and Safety Improvement in Offshore Environments: The BRAM Offshore and Altave Case
records.summary: Abstract This paper explores the utilization of video-based artificial intelligence (AI) tools for enhancing safety measures in offshore environments, specifically within the Bram Offshore fleet in Brazil. The study focuses on the application of AI-powered systems in monitoring and analyzing critical activities, identifying potential risks, and preventing hazardous incidents. It highlights the development and implementation of advanced AI algorithms integrated with video monitoring technology, showcasing their effectiveness in real-time risk detection and mitigation. By monitoring Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) compliance and managing Red Zone areas, these AI solutions significantly improve safety protocols and incident prevention. High-resolution cameras capture detailed images of operations, and the resulting dataset is used to train deep learning algorithms through techniques such as segmentation, classification, object detection, pose estimation, and tracking. Real-time insights are presented on a web platform as alerts, reports, and dashboards, with audible alarms for critical scenarios to ensure immediate interventions. The system's effectiveness is demonstrated through data from the Reedbuck vessel during the last year of operation. Key findings include enhanced hazard detection and improved safety, establishing video-based AI tools as a transformative approach to safety management in the offshore industry.

records.title: Validation of the First Industrial High-Power Laser Perforation Deployment
records.summary: Abstract This paper presents the methods for validating the first successful industrial and field deployment of a high-power laser (HPL) perforating tool. The technology is able to perforate wells without damaging the surrounding substrate's integrity and improving the formation's flow-related properties. Validating the successful operation and the tool's performance is comprehensive and rigorous, relying on qualitative assessments of the data collected from built-in sensors and conventional logs. The accomplishment of the first deployment is a testament to the meticulous research process that has led to the development of the first high-power laser field system. The tool integrates optical, mechanical, and sensing components. The optical and opto-mechanical assembly steers the beam to a target at any azimuthal angle. The sensor array collects data about pressure, temperature, and luminosity that are crucial to monitoring the operation, ensuring the tool's correct functionality, and validating the process. The high-power laser generator is located at the surface and transmitted via fiber-optic cable to the tool in the downhole. The first industrial high-power laser perforation technology was successfully tested and deployed in a cased well; lab and field data proved that the technology could effectively perforate all types of rocks, demonstrating its versatility and adaptability. The tool created several perforations and slots through casing, cement, and formation. The validation of the operation is critical to evaluate the technology's performance and to compare it with current practices (e.g., shaped charges). This assessment used data from routine field measurements and the tool's onboard sensors, including a downhole camera, injectivity test, and sonic and caliper logs. The sensors measured temperature, pressure, and backscattered luminosity. The last is essential to characterize the laser-rock interaction since it is correlated with the effectiveness of the removal process. Temperature readings inside the tool provide information about the health of the optical components. In contrast, the outer temperature and pressure sensors are proxies of the wellbore's flowing dynamics and can help confirm the successful perforation. This HPL perforating method is an innovative and non-explosive alternative to conventional shaped-charge guns. It is cost-effective and enables precise beam control, targeting specific zones and creating enhanced perforation tunnels uninfluenced by the formation's state of stress.

records.title: Utilizing Green-Carbon Nanotubes to Improve Drilling Fluids Rheological Properties: An Experimental Study
records.summary: Abstract A revolutionary technology for turning carbon dioxide into useful products, known as CARGEN®, has been developed at Texas A&M University. The technology features a setup of two reactors linked together, providing a special chance to transform two greenhouse gases, namely methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2), into environmentally friendly carbon nanotubes (GCNTs) and syngas. This research looks into how the newly produced green CNTs affect the flow characteristics of different kinds of water-based drilling fluids, including bentonite mud and brine mud. Various amounts of carbon nanotubes (0.05 w/v %, 0.1w/v %, 0.15 w/v %, and 0.2 w/v%) were tested experimentally to see how they affect the flow characteristics of bentonite mud and brine mud (NaCl). The comparison of properties like plastic viscosity (PV), yield point (YP), and gel strength (GS) was made between the drilling fluids with carbon nanotubes and their control fluids using a rotating viscometer. The tests were carried out at temperatures ranging from 73°F to 200°F. Polyvinyl pyrrolidone (PVP) was employed for GCNT dispersion. The findings show that adding GCNT to water-based drilling fluids changes their rheological properties. For bentonite mud, the PV increased by 13% at 0.05 w/v % GCNT and stayed the same at higher concentrations at room temperature. At higher temperatures (120°F and 150°F), the PV increased with more GCNT, but then decreased at 0.2 w/v %. For brine mud, the PV decreased with more GCNT at higher temperatures, but the GCNT improved the PV more than the control mud, showing better thermal stability. The YP and GS also improved with more GCNT, especially at higher concentrations. These results suggest that GCNT have a significant role in improving the performance and stability of water-based drilling fluids in drilling operations. This research offers valuable insights into the potential use of carbon nanotubes in improving the performance and stability of drilling fluids, contributing to more sustainable industrial practices.

records.title: Utilizing Alpha Amylase as a Substitute for Urease Enzyme in Enzyme-Induced Carbonate Precipitation Solutions for Sand Consolidation in Oil and Gas Wells
records.summary: Abstract Addressing sand production in oil and gas wells is a major challenge, and various methods have been devised to tackle it. However, many of these methods have drawbacks like high costs, slower production rates, or potential damage to the wellbore. Recently, researchers have been exploring enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP) solutions as a solution to consolidate loose sand around the wellbore. Typically, urease is used in EICP solutions to catalyze the hydrolysis of urea. However, due to its costliness, there's a need for alternatives. Alpha amylase has emerged as a potential substitute for urease in EICP solutions. Previous studies have investigated its effectiveness but haven't determined the optimal concentration for complete urease replacement or focused on sand consolidation. Our research successfully identified the optimal concentration of alpha-amylase to entirely replace urease in EICP solutions while achieving effective sand consolidation and maintaining permeability. We comprehensively studied the microstructure and crystal of the precipitates formed SEM. Additionally, sand pack flooding tests were conducted to assess the permeability of the consolidated sand samples. To understand how alpha amylase affects EICP solutions, we prepared a total of 10 solutions for our investigation, among them solutions 1 through 9 are cured at a temperature of 70°C and solution 10 is cured at a temperature 120°C. The first solution served as our baseline, containing 3 g/l of urease enzyme. Solutions 2 through 5 were prepared with both urease enzyme (at a fixed concentration of 1.5 g/l) and varying concentrations of alpha amylase (1.5, 5, 10, and 15 g/l, respectively). Solutions 6 through 9 consisted solely of alpha amylase (without urease enzyme), with concentrations of 3, 5, 10, and 15 g/l. For solution 10, we added 3 g/l of AN 125 (copolymers of AM-AMPS) to solution 7. The solution prepared with 15 g/l of alpha amylase along with 3 g/l urease, showed the highest strength at 1,419 psi. Solution containing 5 g/l of alpha amylase only, exhibited the highest strength at 1,645 psi. Comparatively, the strength of the consolidated sample prepared from the baseline EICP solution was measured at 370 psi. Thus, it's clear that adding 5 g/l of alpha amylase provided the highest strength among all the solutions tested. EICP solution with AN 125 copolymer was cured at high temperature, the consolidated sample showed a strength of 450 psi. The solution with 5 g/l alpha amylase demonstrated the highest strength, further tests were conducted to assess its permeability. It was found that there was only a 20% reduction in permeability after consolidating a sand pack using this solution. This research delivers a novel finding by successfully identifying the optimal concentration of alpha amylase to entirely replace urease enzyme in EICP solutions, enabling effective sand consolidation while maintaining high permeability.

records.title: Utilization of Carbon Dioxide for In-Situ Precipitation of Calcium Carbonate for Conformance Control in Heterogeneous Porous Media
records.summary: Abstract Conformance control is a necessary part of enhanced oil recovery operations in heterogeneous oilfields. However, many techniques center on near-wellbore conformance or are not well suited for low matrix permeability formations. We propose the injection of calcium hydroxide and carbon dioxide as a novel conformance control strategy in reservoirs that experience poor sweep efficiency due to heterogeneity. These two chemical agents react to precipitate solid calcium carbonate, potentially blocking already-swept pores and directing injected fluids to unswept regions of the reservoir. Microfluidic devices (micromodels) were used to perform experiments to observe the fundamental behavior of this reaction in porous media. Precipitation grain size, location, and relative quantity were directly observed while changing injection order, CO2 state, and injection rate. It was found that the reaction took place in porous media for both states of CO2 (gaseous and dissolved in deionized water). Injecting at a lower rate (0.33 ft/day) resulted in less precipitate, but larger grains during single-phase (aqueous) experiments than injecting at a higher rate (1 ft/day). Additionally, more precipitate formed during experiments in which gaseous CO2 was used, compared to when CO2 was dissolved in water. Overall, precipitation occurred where the reactants both contacted each other and mixed, which did not have a preference for high or low permeability zones. Precipitation was also shown to block pore throats in a 2.5D micromodel, reducing the permeability by 92.6% at a 10 ft/day interstitial injection rate. Precipitation via this method can be controlled through CO2 placement in the reservoir and injection rate, as the reaction only occurs where CO2 and Ca(OH)2 are both present and have sufficient convective mixing.

records.title: Use of Machine Learning in Microseismic Monitoring for Thermal Operations in Cold Lake, AB, Canada
records.summary: Abstract This paper presents a novel advancement in the microseismic data processing workflow for monitoring thermal operations at an unconventional bitumen reservoir in Cold Lake, Alberta, Canada. The new enhancement to the monitoring workflow enables fast processing of the microseismic data, by filtering upwards of 94% of noise files from the daily dataset before the files are reviewed and analyzed. The software consists of a deep learning-based application trained to recognize noise files and classify event files according to their predominant source. The tool was deployed in production on an Azure-hosted data manager for almost a year, after extensive testing and achieving adequate level of performance.

records.title: Unveiling the Imprecision in Well Test Data: A Guide to Improve Accuracy of Water Cut Measurement
records.summary: Abstract Well test in Banyu Urip (BU) field employs 2-phase Test Separator equipped with Coriolis Meters to measure gross liquid rate and density for water cut calculation. As BU matures, obtaining water cut data during well test is crucial for well surveillance and scale management. However, there are challenges to precisely and accurately measure water cut as it evolves. This paper shares insights to improve precision and accuracy of water cut measurement during well test. The well test accuracy is validated by comparing produced water (PW) rate from process flow meter at Primary Separators with those derived from Coriolis Meter at Test Separator. The process flow meter's accuracy is ensured through range adjustments following actual rate. In early year, water cut data from Coriolis Meter was inaccurate as indicated by significant PW balance gap. This finding prompted investigation through High-Pressure High-Temperature (HPHT) test analysis, collaboration with manufacturer, and process simulation. Lab test emerged as the primary method to measure water cut by manual sampling at inlet Coriolis Meter during well test. Upon increasing PW rate, discrepancies between PW rate derived from well test manual sampling and process flow meters showed an upswing, reaching 27% gap. This swing was mainly caused by inconsistency in obtaining homogenous oil-water mixture from sampling branch. Hence, examination of Coriolis Meter's accuracy was imperative as it can precisely capture representative sample. An investigation uncovered gas entrainment in preserved liquid sample by testing it in HPHT. The gas lowered actual density from Coriolis Meter below than reference density at the same pressure and temperature, resulting into significant PW balance gap during low water cut operation. Two potential root causes were identified: gas carry under and gas flashing. Vessel sizing verification confirmed adequacy of existing Test Separator in preventing gas carry under, leading to conclusion that gas flashing due to friction loss was the root cause. To address this, the water cut calculation was modified by incorporating an empirical correction factor for gas entrainment, including operation strategy to minimize it. This proved pivotal to improve well test accuracy, reducing PW balance gap to 5%. The improved PW rate precision and accuracy contributed to benefits for well allocation, Voidage Replacement Ratio management, and scale inhibitor effectiveness. Typical gas entrainment issue can be found at liquid leaving separator in saturated condition, thus effecting meter accuracy. Adjusting liquid level upwards can mitigate gas flashing by providing additional static head to compensate friction loss. However, this poses the risk of high-high liquid level trip, especially for slugging well. Therefore, addressing gas entrainment issue by good Test Separator operation strategy and reliable water cut calculation is critical to get accurate and precise well test data.

records.title: Unraveling Damage Variables in Hot Dry Rocks: An Optical Investigation of Geothermal Rocks from UTAH FORGE
records.summary: Abstract Geothermal resources are worldwide renowned for their sustainable and clean attributes. The US Department of Energy (DOE) estimates that harnessing only 0.1% of Earth's geothermal energy could support mankind for two million years. Enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) are highly acclaimed for their ability to extract heat from hot, dry rock. However, issues remain in assuring safe drilling and proper fracturing owing to a lack of knowledge of damage factors and fracture sequences, both of which are crucial for regulating crack propagation. Conventional laboratory approaches often fail to capture the nuanced variation seen in HDR. To address this, the present work uses a three-dimensional optical approach called digital image correlation (3D-DIC) to investigate damage factors in HDR. HDR samples from the DOE UTAH FORGE project's Well 16B (78)-32 are subjected to uniaxial (D 1.5", L 2") and diametrical (D 1.5", L 1") compression using a 100kN precision electro-mechanical load Instron frame at a constant displacement rate of 0.05mm/min. During the uniaxial and diametrical compression studies, a Trilion 3D-DIC image capturing system was used to monitor the samples at a rate of 10 frames per second in a non-contact manner. To monitor deformation during loading, a black-in-white speckle pattern is placed on the specimen. The GOM 3D-DIC system is used to process images, visualize data, and analyze HDR damage variables under various load circumstances. The findings showed that DIC-generated quantitative full-field strain preliminary maps (tension, compression, and shear) include all sequences involved in the damage process as well as discrete strain localization zones (SLZ). Damage factors are quantified using DIC maps to assess sample damage; the tension-compression ratio ranges between 2% and 8%. The damage evolution process of HDR specimens is divided into four phases that are assessed using damage variables: initial damage stage, linear elastic, elastic-plastic, and plastic damage stage. The damage variable regulates the deterioration of the material's stiffness, resulting in a nonlinear relationship between stress and strain. The damage to the SLZ demonstrates that it is bigger than the entire. The damage was at 65% in the yield stage and 35% in the first two stages. The 3D-DIC findings showed that the sample failed when the overall damage variable reached 0.25-0.35, and the damage in the SLZ region reached 0.8-near unity. The damage variable in HDR, which indicates fracture progression, is a unique characteristic in geothermal systems. These results have a substantial impact on our capacity to forecast the damage process in EGS. DIC outperforms CT, SEM, and AE methods in test range, cost-effectiveness, accuracy, and full-field monitoring. It improves our knowledge of damage factors in anisotropic and heterogeneous HDR, increases fracturing efficiency, and improves heat extraction from EGS.

records.title: Unlocking Well Start-Up Uncertainties with Transient Well Flow Modeling
records.summary: Abstract The Absheron field is located offshore Azerbaijan in the Caspian Sea about 100km south-east of Baku and 25km north-east of Shah Deniz field, with a water depth of approximately 500m. After a successful exploration well in 2011 and several development studies, production started in July 2023 through an Early Production Scheme (EPS). This EPS consists of a single subsea well, drilled in 2019, and a 35 km insulated production line going to the existing Oil Rocks facilities. To anticipate the start-up behavior of the Absheron well, Transient Well Flow Modeling simulations integrating the well and the flowline were performed. As such simulations include hydrodynamics (conservation laws for mass, momentum and energy), thermodynamics (fluid description) and thermal exchanges with surroundings (architecture, annulus fluid, rocks…), they enabled the evolution of rates, pressures and temperatures to be predicted for the well ramp-up, in particular to establish the hydrates management procedure. Sensitivities were performed to account for uncertainty on well productivity (from the initial testing and logging data), the wellbore content, chemical injection rates and network pressure. This paper describes the successful work achieved for unlocking challenging uncertainties of Absheron offshore high-pressure gas condensate well start-up. The various sensitivities performed allowed to properly anticipate well behavior. The simulation of several well start-up sequences based on in-house experience, as well as discussions with local offshore teams in charge of operations, helped in establishing operating guidelines grounded on shared understanding and highlighted the main risks linked to the start-up phases. This therefore facilitated the confirmation of the well ramp-up strategy including the expected pressure evolution both at wellhead and at reservoir wellbore interface, as no rate monitoring was available subsea. This ensured well integrity and effective well production. The criticality of hydrates prevention for this high-pressure gas system was handled by optimizing hydrate inhibitor injection rates and flowline pressure. The work performed for this well highlights the benefits of integrated and transverse work and modeling through the integration of both well and flowline to establish optimal and flexible start-up guidelines.

records.title: Unlocking Engineering Solutions for Handling a Complex Mix of KHI, MEG, Corrosion Inhibitor, and Produced Water
records.summary: Abstract The compatibility of KHI and MEG, chemicals used to inhibit gas-hydrate blockage, with corrosion inhibitors (CI) and produced water is a significant concern in the oil and gas industry. Consequently, pipeline integrity, flow assurance, and safely produced water management are critical. This paper highlights an innovative engineering approach based on extensive lab testing and field study that can resolve a complicated mix of KHI, MEG, CI, and produced water. A field sampling was conducted to assess the severity of the mixing of KHI, MEG, and CI and the water produced in the production stream. The tests were conducted at temperatures 35 and 65 oF to reflect summer and winter operations, including the dissolve tendency. The pressure was constant at 70 psi, and the soaking time was 24 hours. Core flood tests were performed using reservoir core plugs to study the compatibility. The incompatibility of KHI, MEG, CI, and produced water was discovered, and the resultant sludge was found to be soluble in distilled water and HCl acid but insoluble in Xylene and Diesel. The core flood test revealed that adding 1,000 ppm of KHI to water will cause the original core brine permeability to decrease by around 13%. There will be a slight decrease in these mixes when the MEG and CI are added. Injection of nearly 7 pore volumes of 7 wt% NaCl brine was able to remove the created damage. The blending of all chemicals with produced water showed less damage (almost 8%) compared to that of KHI alone. Based on this test, the engineering solution is derived from the segregation of the KHI as soon as possible before mixing it with the rest of the water. Therefore, new pipelines, buffer tanks, transfer pumps, and filtration systems are required.

records.title: Unconventional Solutions to Cure Severe-Total Lost Circulations – Field Applications from Middle East
records.summary: Abstract Curing severe to total lost circulation in naturally fractured/vugular formations has always been challenging, especially across the Middle East. In these environments, conventional particulate lost circulation materials (LCMs) are seldom effective due to the uncertainty on the sizes of the formation openings through which losses occur. This paper presents lab evaluation data, supported by field experience, of using a combination high fluid loss squeeze (HFLS) and reticulated foam LCM (RFLCM) treatment. The LCM treatment was designed and qualified based on successful laboratory tests sealing slots up to 40,000 microns. Laboratory and field results are presented from the dual HFLS and RFLCM technology application in two countries in the Middle East: Oman and United Arab Emirates (UAE). The details include formation characteristics, hole size, LCM pill volume and concentrations, and the mixing and pumping methodologies used. The success of the applications is demonstrated by presenting the loss rates before and after applying the treatments, in static and dynamic wellbore conditions, and illustrates savings in terms of rig time. In Oman, the subject wells experienced static losses up to 125 bbls/hr and dynamic losses in the range of 280 bbls/hr (at 550 gpm) to "No returns". The formation was characterized as vugular, and the client's objective was to pump an efficient LCM solution that would cure losses quickly after reaching well Total Depth (TD) and perform logging operations without having to use a cement plug thereby saving rig time. The HFLS and RFLCM treatments were mixed in water, pumped through a circulating sub and a hesitation squeeze was applied. After the squeeze, both static and dynamic loss rates reduced to zero and operations were able to safely continue. For the UAE applications, the subject wells were drilled with non-aqueous fluid and losses experienced were in the range of 85-200 bbls/hr in static conditions, and 150 bbls/hr to complete losses in dynamic mode (990-1250 gpm). The formation was characterized as naturally fractured. The HFLS and RFLCM components were mixed in base oil, pumped through a circulating sub and a hesitation squeeze method was applied. After the squeeze, static losses reduced to 2-15 bbls/hr and dynamic losses to a maximum of 25 bbls/hr (dropping down to 5 bbls/hr while drilling) allowing operations to recommence. In technical qualification tests, plugging of a 40,000-micron lab-simulated fracture/vug opening provided confidence that the subject LCM combination would deal with losses to uncertain fracture/vug size downhole. The successful field applications where severe to total losses were cured has validated the HFLS / RFLCM dual approach. The most notable advantage of improved LCM technology is the reduction in well construction costs through decreased rig time associated with curing severe to total lost circulation.

records.title: Unconventional Field Testing with Clamp-on Multiphase Flowmeter
records.summary: Abstract Following on from a preliminary set of field testing performed at a selection of USA based unconventional wells longer term measurements with a clamp-on Electromagnetic Acoustic Transducer (EMAT) multiphase metering system shall be presented. Longer term trends and correlations between the well behavior and the meter data shall be discussed including opportunities for asset optimization. The clamp-on meter can be rapidly installed on the production flow lines of new wells or retrofitted to existing wells with zero intervention. The EMAT measurement approach is clamp-on and non-radioactive. The workflow used to configure the meter prior to installation to the line shall be described. This includes empirical and physics-based flow analysis of reported well conditions based on pipe geometry, production data and PVT information. Following this, EMAT flowmeters were brought to multiple well sites and installed on producing flowlines downstream of the well heads where measurements were taken. Results obtained were compared against expected flow conditions over longer time periods than previously presented. EMAT flowmeters were installed on several unconventional wells with an installation time less than one hour and with zero intervention. Multiphase flow measurement results from these unconventional wells shall be presented and compared expected well behaviors. The flexibility of the clamp-on deployment allows measurement across multiple wells within a field or reservoir. How this can be applied to real time production optimization and surveillance shall also be explained. In preparation for each well, simulations were performed using the Taitel and Dukler model to predict the flow regime. More detailed physics-based simulations were performed to understand the flow behavior of the individual phases. It is possible with the clamp-on meter to monitor the flow regime and quickly detect flow regime changes within the pipe through monitoring of diagnostic parameters: these shall be compared against the predicted behavior of each of the unconventional wells. Furthermore, the longer-term nature of the measurement allows insight into longer time constant behavior changes of wells and fields leading to further insight into optimization for production and assets. The flexible deployment of the EMAT multiphase flow measurement device presents potential for significant well production and HS&E improvements in oilfield surveillance and production optimization. The longer term assessment of the wells compared to previous measurements with this technology shall allow further insight into longer time constant well- and field-related phenomena which must be understood to effectively optimize production of the well.

records.title: Two-Way Coupled Flow and Geomechanics Simulation with Advanced Dual-Porosity and Dual-Permeability and Local Grid Refinement for Shale Primary Depletion
records.summary: Abstract This paper represents a new two-way coupled flow and geomechanical simulation model that utilizes an Advanced Dual Porosity Dual Permeability (A-DPDK) model with local grid refinement (LGR). A hydraulic fracture's conductivity is strongly dependent on the effective stress on fracture face. During production, increased effective stress could cause proppant embedment, crushing, and fracture closure. Coupled flow and geomechanical simulation is critical to capture the fracture conductivity changes with stress and perform accurate production forecast. The geomechanical problem with the DPDK can be solved with the constitutive equations for stress and porosity of multiple porosity systems. A fractured reservoir contains different regions in the fracture domain, for example, propped, unpropped, and natural fractures which have different mechanical properties. Our proposed model mathematically represents mapping of mechanical properties in different regions of fracture and matrix domains. In addition, we showed the mapping between a LGR flow system and a non-LGR geomechanical system. We demonstrated a realistic fracture geometry with the A-DPDK LGR system. We validated the numerical convergence of the A-DPDK with LGR by performing grid size sensitivity tests in flow and mechanical grids. The proposed simulation model was applied to oil production from a shale and tight (S&T) reservoir. The proposed simulation approach can model total stress update near fractures more realistically. The new stress and pressure results obtained from the integrated flow and geomechanics workflow allowed us to incorporate stress impact from the depletion of a different bench and the resulting fracture azimuth change. The combination of a LGR flow system and a non-LGR geomechanical system supports reasonable computational time even with two-way coupling simulation, which encourages us to adopt the new simulation approach for modeling oil production and evaluating stress change.

records.title: Two-Step Process to Quantify Effects of Geological and Completion Parameters on Unconventional Well Performance
records.summary: Abstract Machine learning algorithms have been frequently used to evaluate the performance of unconventional wells. Typically, all available features (geological and completion) are used to correlate the data to production performance of wells. Unlike the traditional approach, we correlate production data first to geological and geophysical parameters (depth, porosity, permeability, brittleness, etc.). We then take the residual information after the first correlation and correlate the residual to completion parameters such as length, proppant amount and fracturing fluid. By separating geology from completion, we can isolate the effect of geology removed from completion. This is very useful for exploration prospects where very limited or no data are available from existing wells. Further, by correlating completion parameters separately to residual values, we can quantify the impact of each completion parameter which can help optimize completion parameters to get the most benefit of various completion strategies. We use SHAP (Shapley Additive Prediction) to isolate the effects of each completion parameter. Using large, confidential, data available, we evaluated multiple basins and applied the proposed methodology. These include: Eagleford, and Marcellus Basins. What we observed, in general, is that approximately 70 % of the variance in production data can be explained by geological parameters and about 20 % of the variance can be explained by completion parameters. True vertical depth consistently ranked as the most important geological feature in predicting performance, but other features varied in importance. If appropriate analog can be understood, the methodology from mature formations can be used in exploration blocks to identify sweet spots. The evaluation of completion parameters revealed that the relationship between performance and completion is not always linear and in some instances, incremental benefits of larger completion inputs are negligible and counter-productive. The length of the well is the most important completion variable in determining the performance. The impact of individual parameters varies depending on production parameter selected. Geology becomes increasingly important as more production data are added (12 month vs 24 month vs EUR) and completion parameters are less able to explain the performance as the length of the production data increases.

records.title: Triaxial Hydraulic-Mechanical-Chemical Coupled Experiments for Hydrocarbon Production in Unconventional Shale Reservoirs
records.summary: Abstract Unconventional oil and gas play a key role in the global transition to clean energy. Advances in horizontal drilling and hydraulic fracturing have enabled substantial hydrocarbon extraction from shale formations. However, the initial high production rates from these formations are not sustained over time, leading to a significantly lower recovery rates compared to conventional reservoirs. Hydrocarbon production in shale formations is governed by complex, multi-physical coupled mechanisms, including fluid diffusion in the tight matrix, multiphase flow in fractures, and stress dependent interactions between matrix and fracture. To address these challenges, we developed a high pressure ‘quad-pore’ triaxial cell and an in situ experimental protocol to simulate the live oil production scenarios. Under fully in-situ conditions, we saturated Wolfcamp shale with live oil, induced fractures, and conducted soaking, pressure drawdown, long term production, and stress dependent permeability evaluation. Through multiple tests, we found that shale gas production is mainly driven by pressure drawdown, long term production, and fracturing, while oil production was mainly produced during the long-term production and pressure drawdown. Soaking enhances hydrocarbon production through imbibition. Complex, branched fractures with larger surface areas are more effective in producing shale gas. As pressure decreases, the produced hydrocarbons becomes heavier, with higher concentrations of intermediate-chain and longer-chain hydrocarbons. Heavier oil dominates in the late production stage. The bubble point marks a critical threshold, beyond which a large amount of oil and gas are produced. These findings promote the development of a better strategy for unconventional oil and gas production and contribute to achieving important economic, energy security, and environmental benefits.

records.title: Trends in Academic Research and Graduate Education in Petroleum Engineering Programs
records.summary: Abstract Undergraduate education in Petroleum Engineering (PE) has survived the latest downturn in the industry, and enrollment has started to show an uptick in numbers. Anecdotal evidence, however, has been hinting at a different trend in graduate training and academic research. In this work, the authors collected and analyzed data, on US-based petroleum engineering departments, that included over $137M in external research funding and over 1,900 thesis/dissertations over the span of ten years, in addition to over 1,100 publications from these departments in 2023. The data was analyzed through classification into different categories, including Reservoir/Production, Fracturing, Drilling, Non-Fossil Fuel Geoenergy (geothermal, CCS/CCUS, hydrogen), and Others. The results reveal a drastic shift in research and graduate training that is expected to significantly impact the future of these departments and the workforce they train. The findings show a drop of 70% in external funding supporting oil and gas research over the past ten years, and a growth of 230% in funding for non-fossil fuel topics. This transition is shown to have impacted the topics represented in theses, dissertations, and publications. The findings call for strategic discussions around alignment between the needs and the trajectories in this domain.

records.title: Transforming Pneumatic Methane Emissions Mitigation While Leveraging IRA Energy Credit
records.summary: Abstract Natural gas-driven pneumatic controllers used in onshore oil and gas operations account for approximately 43% of all production-related methane emissions in the U.S., primarily due to their deployment in remote areas without access to electric grids. These controllers, essential for process flow and overpressure prevention, have historically lacked technological advancements and commercial solutions for methane emission reduction due to their widespread and remote distribution, the absence of readily available power sources, and the critical impact on operational integrity. The EPA's NSPS OOOO(b) and OOOO(c) regulations, effective as of May 2024, impose strict standards on methane and VOC emissions from pneumatic devices and pumps. The regulations require new and modified pneumatic controllers to achieve zero emissions, with specific guidelines for existing sources, emphasizing monitoring, recordkeeping, and advanced leak detection technologies. These regulations reflect a significant shift towards mitigating the environmental impact of methane emissions from these devices. Current technologies for emission reduction, including compressed instrument air, electrically powered pneumatic devices, vapor recovery units, and liquified nitrogen, often fall short due to high costs, efficiency losses, and reliance on environmentally harmful energy sources. Renewable energy solutions, though promising, face economic and efficiency barriers, particularly in remote locations. To address the gaps, Blue Mountain Operations developed a new generation of solar-powered instrument air compressors and pumps leveraging high-efficiency Permanent Magnet Synchronous AC (PMAC) motors and VFD controller. This system achieves high electromechanical efficiency and reliability, significantly reducing methane emissions and operational costs while ensuring robust performance in remote settings. The Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) of 2022 enhanced the Federal Investment Tax Credit (ITC), providing substantial financial incentives for renewable energy projects. In 2023, an oil and gas operator in the Uintah Basin implemented the above-mentioned solar solutions replacing 905 methane-emitting pneumatic pumps in a USD 10.5 million project. This transition qualified for the full 30% ITC and an additional 10% bonus, generated USD 2.8 million in tax credits and demonstrated a viable path for the oil and gas industry to achieve substantial financial and environmental benefits. Two case studies presented in the paper illustrate the deployment and performance of the PMAC compressor solutions in the Permian and Uintah Basins, demonstrating significant methane emission reductions, cost savings, and enhanced operational efficiency. These projects, supported by financial incentives such as the Federal Investment Tax Credit (ITC) and the Inflation Reduction Act, highlight the economic and environmental benefits of transitioning to sustainable technologies in the oil and gas industry.

records.title: Transfer Learning in Subsurface Flow Surrogate Model with Physics-Guided Neural Network
records.summary: Abstract It is a great challenge for reservoir engineers to accurately and quickly model the subsurface flow surrogate for oil and gas reservoirs. The traditional numerical simulation methods are high computational complexity and time-consuming. The widely used pure data- driven flow surrogate methods require massive high-quality data due to lack of theoretical foundation. Therefore, it is necessary to develop transfer learning methods integrating prior knowledge with data-driven deep learning methods to solve complex seepage problems. To reduce data requirements and improving modeling efficiency, a theory-guided and data-driven transfer learning method is proposed to build the fast and accurate subsurface flow surrogate model. Specifically, a data-driven machine learning method is first proposed to simulate and predict the flow processes and build the primary surrogate model. In addition, physical mechanism and constraints are embedded into the data-driven model to make the prediction results satisfy the prior domain knowledge. The transfer learning method based on physics-guided neural network (TL-PG) integrates the seepage theory with sparse spatial data to improve the prediction accuracy of the surrogate model. The proposed TL-PG method is verified by a subsurface flow problem in heterogeneous reservoir models. First, we build a flow field to simulate 50 years of production history. A physics-guided neural network model is trained based on the samples from the first 30 years and tested based on the last 20 years of data. The relative L2 loss and the coefficient of determination R2 are used for comparison. Compared with the purely data-driven method, the relative L2 loss of physics-guided neural network is increased by 16%, and the mean coefficient of determination R2 is up to 0.8932, which means the embedded physical mechanism can greatly improve the performance of neural networks. Secondly, the physics-guided neural network is selected as the pre-training model. Then, the random points from the year 31 to 40 are used to fine-tune the model. Finally, the TL-PG surrogate model is validated by the last 10 years of data. The mean coefficient of determination R2 is up to 0.9522, which has improved by 25% compared to purely data-driven deep neural network (DNN) method, and only when the number of training data and epochs are increased several times, the performance can be comparable to the TL-PG method.
